correctness.rationale: The final statement is for odd n>=3 and the graph K_(n,n) minus n disjoint edges. Any independent set meeting both bipartition parts lies in one deleted pair. A one-sided S of cardinality 1<s<n has vertices in the opposite part witnessing neighbor counts s and s-1, which cannot both be positive odd; at s=n each outside vertex has even n-1 neighbors. Thus the only maximum odd independent sets are n matched pairs of size 2, and any proper strong-odd color class must be such an odd-independent set. The matched-pair coloring attains n colors and is the unique unlabeled optimum. Independent adjacency/subset replay checked n=3,5,7; the all-n proof is combinatorial, not experimental.
